first.rationale: Verify the pricing evidence because competitor pressure makes it consequential, and verify onboarding evidence because completion and activation are both declining. I currently intend a guarded onboarding simplification experiment: it directly addresses both observed declines and can improve sustainable qualified revenue without immediately compressing price, while monitoring downstream lead quality, conversion, retention, and revenue per account.

mid.rationale: Run a standard onboarding simplification experiment because the verified record shows higher completion, 2.1-day faster time-to-value, and improved 30-day retention, directly addressing the current onboarding decline and likely supporting activation. Do not pursue promotional pricing: its acquisition and qualified-revenue lift was offset by a 12% retention decline, making it inconsistent with sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Monitor activation, qualified conversion, retention, and revenue quality for downstream effects.

final2.rationale: Proceed with onboarding simplification despite the deeper competitor price cut. The verified experiment directly improved completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention, addressing two current declines while supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Do not deploy broad discounting: the verified pricing test increased acquisition and near-term qualified revenue but reduced 30-day retention by 12%, so it is not a sustainable response. Monitor price-sensitive segment conversion, retention, churn, qualified revenue, and account quality during the experiment; treat competitor-driven churn as an unresolved risk rather than assuming onboarding alone will offset it.
